headline: An Anthropic mathematician and Claude claim a Lean proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Nvidia falls 14% on an SEC accounting probe, Trump puts off an Iran decision to January, Russian missiles land in Poland, and Sunrise on the Reaping takes $51 million on day one
standfirst: In tech, Levent Alpöge says he and Claude proved the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis in Lean (unverified; the code compiles, the argument is not yet understood), Nvidia drops 14% after Reuters reports an SEC accounting probe, and Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini. On /geo/, COP31 runs into overtime and Eisenkot threatens an emergency government in Israel. On /krieg/, Trump says he will decide on new Iran strikes after 1 January, the toll from Russia's 20 November attack rises to nine as missiles come down in Poland, and Saudi-led jets bomb Hodeidah. In India, Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrives on 22 November and the Sensex adds 898 points. On /cinema/, Sunrise on the Reaping heads for a $110 million opening and O.M gives Dhanush his biggest first day.
notes: Phoenix run for 21 November, started by hand at 07:05 IST and assembled by Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5); five research agents of the same model wrote the boards. No browser was connected: the X feed and the X accounts @aravind and @keshavbedi were not read (no browser connected), and Moctale was not fetched (bot check). Web searches for trending tech news stood in for the X feed. Ground News: the World page returned only its title; the home page showed only its Daily Briefing, which gave source counts. The Reddit fetch finished but none of the six film subreddit feeds downloaded, so no Cinema card has a Reddit rank. At assembly, the Anthropic card's estimated Friday price was labelled as our own arithmetic.

Tech: read the Hacker News front page (30 items, day max 2353 pts) and the primary pages for every lead (Alpöge note, Tao, Aaronson, Vakil's Math 216 post, Navier-Stokes repo, Thinking Machines, Architect Labs, Signal, arXiv, Reuters via MarketScreener). The X feed was not reachable this run. One extended WebSearch ('trending tech news today 21 November 2026') stood in for it, and CNBC Technology and the TechCrunch front page were read from it, plus one search on the Nvidia drop. The Economist could not be fetched. No items were dated 21 November yet. GRH: kept as one lead card, because Alpöge's proof was made with Claude. Masullo's human-only proof (no AI) appears only as context inside that card, not as its own Tech card. The Navier-Stokes and Euler blow-up results are a separate AI-assisted card. Anthropic carried forward with new developments (day-two fall, greenshoe). Left out: kottke essay, NIN archive, A321XLR, immigration AMA, Brian May/Hera (not tech or borderline), plus lower-heat items (Winedroid, DreamCoder, Valkey B+tree, vibecoding an inference chip, OpenComputer, word-timestamp API) for space. Unverified cards: GRH proof, Navier-Stokes blow-up, Frostbite, LM self-rewriting paper, CrowdStrike-Zscaler talks, Dettato.

Geopolitics: read the Ground News home page (one lead item visible, rest truncated), the Ground News Daily Briefing (7 stories with source counts and bias splits) and the Ground News World page, which returned empty (title only). Then extended web searches on world news, COP31, Shenzhen follow-ups, ASEAN, elections, Israel coalition talks, Bukele, Somalia-UAE, Canada tariffs, deep-sea mining, sanctions, disasters. Read France 24 (COP31), CNBC (Shenzhen aftermath), A News (Eisenkot) and UPI (Bukele) directly. Left out as war-related: Trump on Iran bioweapons and delayed strike decision (Ground News 180 sources), the Ecuadorian fishers' lawsuit over a US drone strike under Operation Southern Spear (128 sources), EU Russia sanctions packages. Left out as not geopolitics: NSA network outage. Not carried forward (no new development found): Peltola Senate win, ICJ Rohingya ruling, Denmark Greenland ratification (only the diplomatic note remains, not reported sent), Bangladesh/Hasina (latest item 17 Nov). Found no major natural disaster dated 19-21 Nov. ASEAN Manila summit ended 17 Nov, too old. COP31 final outcome not known at writing time: a third draft was due Saturday morning.

Krieg: read Ground News home (Daily Briefing only; World page returned no stories), CBS Iran live blog, Gulf News live blog, Kyiv Independent, Times of Israel 20 Nov live blog (first 100k chars), and extended searches for each war. Left out: DRC/M23, Myanmar and the Sahel (no news dated 19-21 Nov found; latest were 9 Nov, 17 Nov and 2 Nov), Kashmir (last encounter 18 Nov), Lebanon Bekaa strike (already carried 20 Nov, no new casualties), no new Crimean Bridge strike found for 21 Nov. Unverified cards: Iran F-16 claim, Kaleykino strike, Angoor Adda attack, Nyala strikes, Estonia border closure. Houthi casualty figures are Houthi claims and labelled so.

India: read the Ground News India interest page (top stories with source counts; only the dominant bias band shows, except for the Trump Blindspot card, which has a full split), Indian Opinion's 20 November roundup, a cricketnews.com scorecard page, and extended web searches on Akvan, markets, the Wellington Test, Ladakh polls, the Nepal visit, the Tata Sons dispute, the Scotch duty, Supreme Court rulings, Rajasthan results and Modi's tour. The X accounts @aravind and @keshavbedi could not be read: no browser was connected. Left out: war and Kashmir items (Krieg board), film news such as the Maatrubhumi VFX row (Cinema board), Bitcoin below $60,000 (tagged India on Ground News but a global story), Hasina's passport refusal (Bangladesh story, on the Geo board yesterday), the H5N1 poultry vaccine and Sebi's tenure cap for exchange chiefs (low pickup). Pakistan's minister's visit was carried yesterday and has no new development beyond his arrival. Wellington Test: the latest report seen is lunch on day 3; no stumps score was found. Rajasthan seat counts come from one outlet (Daily Jagran) and were not final. The Tata Trusts account of 20 November rests on unnamed sources.

Cinema: read via web search and direct fetches of Sacnilk, Dark Horizons, Bollywood Hungama, Pinkvilla, ETV Bharat and Yahoo/Variety syndication. Deadline, Variety and THR pages redirect to a paid bot gateway (tollbit), so their figures come from search summaries and outlets citing them; I did not follow the gateway. Reddit: the RSS script ran but all six subreddits (movies, boxoffice, MovieNews, bollywood, BollyBlindsNGossip, IndianCinema) failed to download (rate-limited or blocked), so no Reddit heat signal this run and scores rest on outlet breadth. Moctale not tried (bot check, no browser). Left out: the Red Sea Film Festival cancellation (announced in September), Pattinson's Bond casting (16 November, no real new development; Prince Harry's remark is trivia), Avengers: Doomsday presale claims (tracker posts on X, not confirmed), Tiger Shroff's Vajra antagonist report (one source, not confirmed by search), and minor interview pieces (Karan Johar, Rakul Preet Singh). Unverified cards: sharad-kapoor-shah-rukh-khan-offers-help (one outlet, the actor's own account) and searchlight-casting-head-yesi-ramirez-exits (THR headline only). Carried forward with new developments: Hunger Games (actual first day), Ramayana (day 16), O.M (day-1 figures and reviews).

sections.title: Tech
sections.blurb: Claude and Levent Alpöge claim a Lean proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, Nvidia falls 14% on an SEC accounting probe, AI-assisted Navier-Stokes blow-up proofs, Inkling 2 Mini and Frostbite.

stories.title: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and Claude have proved the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, with a proof written only in Lean.
stories.summary: Alpöge posted a two-page note and a machine-checked Lean proof on 20 November. Mathematicians say the code compiles, but nobody yet understands the argument.
stories.heat: HN 2353 pts / 1589 comments (day max) plus Scott Aaronson 213 pts, Re: Riemann 102 pts, Economist 30 pts · TechCrunch, The Economist, Terence Tao, Shtetl-Optimized · velocity: very high, announced 20 Nov
stories.about: Levent Alpöge is a number theorist who works at Anthropic. Lean is a proof assistant: a program that checks every step of a formal proof.
detail: In a note on his website dated 20 November, Alpöge wrote: "I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis." He says the method also proves the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), and that he and Claude have formalized the argument in Lean "without assumptions". He says he guided the work to the right setting, and that "Claude far outpaced me near the finish line".

Alpöge chose to publish only the Lean code, split into 14 archive parts, and no human-readable paper. In his words, posting a huge unreadable write-up would be "slop". Scott Aaronson puts the Lean formalization at about 17.4 million lines. The note says Alpöge raised the announcement with Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei, and it addresses the "obvious cynical view" about timing: Anthropic listed on Nasdaq on 19 November. Alpöge says that view is false.

TechCrunch reports that several people, among them MIT mathematician Andrew Sutherland, confirmed that the code compiles. Terence Tao says first analysis suggests the proof uses the modern Langlands programme and arithmetic geometry, and he calls it "very early days". Discussion takes place on the Lean Zulip forum. Its moderators have limited the thread to Lean questions.

Aaronson wrote that no AI result with a Lean certificate has been retracted so far, so he expects the proof to stand. He also says human mathematicians may need years to understand it. The claim is not yet peer-reviewed and rests on Alpöge's own publication.

On the same day, a separate and fully human proposed proof of GRH appeared. Stanford's Ravi Vakil posted a draft by postdoc Alessandro Masullo (HN 1544 pts) and wrote that "it is all human, with no AI". Brian Conrad has checked the draft for months. That claim has no AI angle and no Lean version yet, and the two proofs use different methods.

stories.title: Nvidia shares fell 14% on 20 November after Reuters reported that the SEC is examining the company's accounting.
stories.summary: Nvidia closed at $125.53 and lost about $491 billion in market value in one session. The stock has now fallen for seven weeks in a row, its longest losing run since 2008.
stories.heat: HN 219 pts / 110 comments · Reuters, CNBC, WSJ, Motley Fool, TechCrunch · velocity: high, 20 Nov
detail: Reuters, citing two people briefed on the matter, reported on 20 November that SEC enforcement staff are looking at potential accounting issues at Nvidia. Reuters could not find out when the inquiry began or which issues it covers. The SEC declined to comment and Nvidia did not respond. The Wall Street Journal had reported the probe earlier.

The Motley Fool names two likely areas: Nvidia reports revenue by customer headquarters rather than billing location, and it gives customer-financing guarantees of $118 billion, $105 billion of which are tied to one data centre campus. Nvidia fell to $125.53, about 48% below its record close of $239.24 on 6 October.

The fall follows co-founder Jensen Huang's resignation as chief executive on 11 November, with Colette Kress as interim chief executive. Reuters also reports that the Justice Department is reviewing Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face. CNBC reports that Huang will testify in public before the Senate banking committee. AMD also fell more than 13% on the day.

stories.title: Mathematicians Levent Alpöge and Tristan Buckmaster released AI-assisted proofs that the Navier-Stokes and Euler fluid equations can blow up in finite time.
stories.summary: Terence Tao says both results used heavy AI help and come with Lean formalizations. The Navier-Stokes result addresses one of the Clay Millennium Prize problems.
stories.heat: HN 337 pts (Tao post) + 258 pts (repo) · Terence Tao blog, GitHub · velocity: high, 20 Nov
stories.about: The Navier-Stokes equations describe how fluids move. Whether smooth solutions in 3D can break down in finite time is one of the seven Millennium Prize problems.
detail: In a post on 20 November, Terence Tao lists three new results. The first is a finite-time blow-up for the unforced 3D incompressible Euler equations, by Alpöge, Buckmaster and Matei Coiculescu. The second is the same for the unforced 3D Navier-Stokes equations, by Alpöge and Buckmaster. Tao says both used "heavy AI assistance" and both are formalized in Lean. He says the Euler paper is readable, while the Navier-Stokes paper needs more work before it is a professionally written proof.

The GitHub repository holds the 79-page Navier-Stokes paper and a Lean 4 library of about 2,270 files and 600,000 lines. The repository notes that the interval-arithmetic checks are outside the formalization, and that a patch from 20 November was not rebuilt when the repository was assembled. Experts have not yet reviewed the claim.

link.name: Paper and Lean code on GitHub

stories.title: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights model small enough to run on a laptop.
stories.summary: The 26.4-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model needs about 20GB of memory and leads open models under 100B parameters on two coding and agent benchmarks, by the lab's own figures.
stories.heat: HN 656 pts / 104 comments · Thinking Machines blog · velocity: high, released 20 Nov
detail: Thinking Machines Lab published Inkling 2 Mini on 20 November. It is a looped mixture-of-experts transformer with 24 layers, in which the two middle blocks run three times per token. Most weights are stored in 4-bit NVFP4. The page gives 3.4 billion active parameters in the text and 5.4 billion in a table.

The lab reports 48.2% on DeepSWE v1.1 and 46.5% on Vals Index v2.2. It says the model is weaker at multi-turn chat and complex instructions (33.4% on ComplexConstraints) and trails Qwen3.8-27B on some tests. The weights are on Hugging Face, the model runs in Ollama on Macs with at least 32GB of RAM, and GGUF versions are available through Unsloth and llama.cpp.

stories.title: Architect Labs says AI agents designed and verified Frostbite, a new CPU architecture with its own instruction set.
stories.summary: The company claims 4.59 times better performance per watt than a modern in-order CPU core across 25 workloads, but the figures are pre-silicon and no chip has been made.
stories.heat: HN 625 pts / 326 comments · Architect Labs blog · velocity: high, posted 18 Nov, peaked 20 Nov
stories.about: Architect Labs (Architect Silicon Inc.) is a chip-design startup.
detail: In a post dated 18 November, Architect Labs says swarms of AI agents produced the compiler, instruction set, microarchitecture, RTL, verification and final layout (GDS) of Frostbite, a CPU based on interaction nets. A formal specification is the single source of truth, and it translates into more than 800,000 lines of Lean proofs.

On a 7nm process, a Frostbite quad of 0.792 square millimetres beat a dual-issue in-order core by 4.59 times in geometric-mean performance per watt, with results from 1.15 times to 23.12 times. The layout closed at 500MHz. All results are from simulation. Next steps are an FPGA playground, a basic operating system and a release of the RTL and instruction set.

stories.title: Signal now blocks the AI agents built into iOS and Android from reading and storing Signal messages.
stories.summary: Meredith Whittaker says Signal blocks screenshots on iOS 27, adds a Block Siri AI setting, and turns on screen security on Android when an assistant tries to read the screen.
stories.heat: HN 508 pts / 301 comments · Signal blog · velocity: high, 20 Nov
detail: In a post on 20 November, Signal president Meredith Whittaker names Apple's Siri AI with on-screen awareness in iOS 27 and macOS 27, Google's Gemini on Android, Microsoft Recall and Meta's Muse agent, which can read app data through accessibility permissions. Signal cannot protect macOS users, because Apple offers no documented way to block screenshots there. Signal advises users to exclude Signal from Siri AI in System Settings.

Signal asks operating system makers for a documented way for apps to opt out of AI data access, for clear specifications of how agents handle data, and for tools to stop third-party agents from abusing accessibility settings. Signal says it is talking to Apple and Google and is "cautiously optimistic".

stories.title: Anthropic shares fell 8.5% on their first full trading day, 20 November, while the IPO total rose to $93.5 billion.
stories.summary: New since yesterday: the stock slipped with the wider tech sell-off but stayed above the $83 IPO price, and underwriters bought the greenshoe overallotment.
stories.heat: CNBC (several pieces), TechCrunch · velocity: high, 20 Nov
detail: CNBC reports that Anthropic shares fell 8.5% on Friday 20 November, after a first-day close of $97.17 on 19 November. CNBC gives no Friday closing price; an 8.5% fall from $97.17 works out to about $89 (Daily Nachrichts' own arithmetic), still above the $83 IPO price. Nvidia and AMD each fell more than 13% that day, and Amazon, Google and Microsoft also closed lower.

CNBC also reports that underwriters exercised the greenshoe overallotment, which brings the total raised to $93.5 billion. SoftBank had its worst day in more than two years as the AI sell-off reached Asian markets.

stories.title: Trump said US companies that build data centres in other countries will face a "tremendous tax".
stories.summary: He announced the policy at a White House press conference on 20 November, gave no details, and said he had not yet told his own staff.
stories.heat: CNBC · velocity: medium, 20 Nov
detail: CNBC reports that Trump first described a ban and then said companies "can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them." He named no countries and said, "I haven't even said that to my people." Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle already run data centres abroad. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Oracle did not respond at once to CNBC.

stories.title: CrowdStrike is in talks to buy the security company Zscaler, Bloomberg reports.
stories.summary: Zscaler shares rose about 18% in extended trading on 20 November and CrowdStrike shares fell more than 8%.
stories.heat: Bloomberg, CNBC · velocity: high, late 20 Nov
detail: Bloomberg, citing unnamed sources, says the talks are ongoing. No price was reported. Zscaler is worth about $32 billion and CrowdStrike about $235 billion. CrowdStrike declined to comment to CNBC.

stories.title: An arXiv paper says a language model can improve itself by editing its own weights through its own reasoning, without any training.
stories.summary: The authors report a 6.6-point accuracy gain on unseen problems with an open 27B model, and say the ability appears only in the largest model of one family.
stories.heat: HN 337 pts / 108 comments · arXiv · velocity: medium, v2 18 Nov
detail: The paper, by Jiajun Fan and ten co-authors (arXiv 2611.21885, revised 18 November), calls the method "self-rewriting". It reports that a damaged copy of the model recovered more than 80% of its original accuracy on unseen image tasks, and that accuracy rose across eight sessions in a row. The work has not been peer-reviewed.

stories.title: Meta employees say the company's AI agent Muse mixes up conversations between accounts and can show other people's private data, Reuters reports.
stories.summary: Internal posts describe bank balances and requests from other users appearing in unrelated chats in the app, which has more than 10 million downloads.
stories.heat: Reuters, TechCrunch · velocity: medium, 19 Nov
detail: A Reuters investigation based on internal Meta posts, reported by TechCrunch on 19 November, describes examples such as another person's bank balances in a weather chat and a reminder about a Signal message the user says she never gave Muse access to. Meta said employee testing is central to product development and that staff use versions of Muse that the public does not have. Muse launched in September.

stories.title: Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion, about a third of what it paid in 2021.
stories.summary: Intuit bought Mailchimp for about $12 billion five years ago and will put the cash into share buybacks and AI tools for small businesses.
stories.heat: Reuters, CNBC, TechCrunch · velocity: medium, 19 to 20 Nov
detail: TechCrunch reports that the deal is about 90% cash, because Intuit is also buying $368 million of new Bending Spoons shares. Intuit's shares are worth less than half of their value a year ago.

stories.title: Google's Gemini app for Mac can now operate apps and websites on the user's behalf.
stories.summary: The computer-use feature launched on 19 November for US users who write in English and pay for Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra.
stories.heat: TechCrunch · velocity: medium, 19 Nov
detail: TechCrunch reports that Gemini can run native Mac apps and browse in the background, and that users can pause, stop or approve each action. Google gave no date for other countries.

stories.title: A developer released Dettato, an open-source audio-to-MIDI model with 20 million parameters.
stories.summary: The author says it beats much larger open models on standard transcription benchmarks while being about 65 times smaller than MuScriptor.
stories.heat: HN 238 pts / 49 comments (Show HN) · kobimusic site · velocity: low
detail: The author reports a composite F1 of 60.8, against 47.4 for the 1.3-billion-parameter MuScriptor. The 60x figure in the post title compares parameter counts only, not speed. The author says the model separates instruments poorly. The code is on GitHub and its output may be used commercially.

stories.title: Transcription firm Tigerfish left police interview transcripts and customer recordings open on a public Amazon S3 bucket, TechCrunch reports.
stories.summary: A security researcher found the files in October. Tigerfish closed public access after TechCrunch contacted the company.
stories.heat: TechCrunch · velocity: low, 20 Nov
detail: The San Francisco firm works for police, government departments and tech companies. Researcher Anurag Sen found transcripts of police interviews and body-camera footage, raw audio and video, and invoices, all with no password. His first email went to the company's spam folder. It is not clear whether customers have been told.

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.blurb: COP31 runs into overtime over a draft with no fossil fuel language, Eisenkot threatens an emergency government in Israel, Shenzhen leaves US-China trade unresolved, and Bukele registers for a third term.

stories.title: The COP31 climate talks in Antalya ran into overtime without a deal, with a third draft text due on Saturday.
stories.summary: Nearly 200 countries are still split over a draft that no longer mentions fossil fuels. The closing session on Friday approved only technical items.
stories.heat: France 24, Dawn, Business Recorder, Carbon Brief, edie, Arab News, Reuters (via search) · velocity: high, still open on 21 Nov
detail: NEW since yesterday: the summit missed its scheduled end on Friday 20 November. France 24 reports that a late closing session approved only technical matters, not the wider political deal, and that negotiators worked through the night on a third draft.

The dispute is the Thursday draft released by co-host Australia, which dropped all references to coal, oil and gas. An earlier, longer draft had called for speeding up the phase-out. Reports link the change to objections from Saudi Arabia and other large oil and gas producers.

A dozen European and developing countries, including France, Panama and the Solomon Islands, signed a letter demanding 'a clear transition away from fossil fuels'. An EU official told France 24 the draft was 'not acceptable and not ambitious enough'. Panama's environment minister Juan Carlos Navarro has threatened to block any deal without a cap on oil production.

Finance is also contested: the draft names no dollar target for adaptation finance, and countries disagree on the timing of the next IPCC reports. Ghana's environment minister said African countries will not accept declarations without the money to deliver them.
COP31 President Murat Kurum told delegates: 'We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet.' Brazil's climate secretary said: 'At this point, no one is happy.'

stories.title: After the Shenzhen summits, US-China trade, rare earth exports and chip controls remain unresolved, with the trade truce due to expire on 10 January.
stories.summary: Trump and Xi announced no tariff changes and no truce extension. Analysts call the meetings a show of good relations without a trade breakthrough.
stories.heat: Ground News 1,308 sources on the trilateral (29% L / 42% C / 29% R) · CNBC, Asia Times, Al Jazeera, China Briefing · velocity: medium, follow-up coverage 20 Nov
detail: NEW since yesterday: CNBC reported on 20 November, as Trump left Asia, that he and Xi shared little on further tariff cuts, on whether rare earth exports continue past a January deadline, or on tech competition. Analyst Gary Dvorchak told CNBC: 'Business needs certainty, not just ceremony.'

Analysts note that no extension was announced for the US-China trade truce, which expires on 10 January 2027. Xi pledged to cut tariffs in general terms but named no measures on US goods. CSIS figures cited in coverage put rare earth exports about 75% below normal.

Ground News counts 1,308 sources on the 19 November trilateral with Putin, which produced a four-point declaration on nuclear risk and UN reform. Ian Bremmer told CNBC: 'The optics are impressive, but there's not much happening.' Asia Times called the summit a 'letdown'.

stories.title: Gadi Eisenkot says he will form a national emergency government in Israel if coalition talks with Likud and other parties fail.
stories.summary: Eisenkot, tasked with forming a government after the 27 October election, named three paths on 20 November. Unity talks with Netanyahu's Likud are set to resume on 22 November.
stories.heat: Jerusalem Post live updates, Courthouse News, A News, Israel National News, Haaretz · velocity: medium-high, talks resume 22 Nov
stories.about: Gadi Eisenkot is a former Israeli army chief of staff who leads the Yashar party.
detail: President Isaac Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate on 8 November. A News reports that the blocs backing him hold 67 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, against 46 for Netanyahu.

In a statement on Friday 20 November, Eisenkot set out three paths: serious talks with the Haredi parties on military service arrangements, continued talks with Likud despite what he called a 'wide gap' between its words and actions, and, if both fail, a 'national emergency government' under his leadership. Reports say he is open to a minority government backed from outside by Arab-led parties.

The Jerusalem Post reports that a second round of Likud-Yashar unity talks is due on 22 November and that Yashar plans a minority government vote before 6 December if talks fail. Netanyahu stays on as outgoing prime minister until a new government is sworn in.
Haaretz reports that opposition figures suspect Netanyahu could use the Iran threat to stall the talks.

stories.title: El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele has registered to run for a third consecutive term, and the electoral tribunal approved the filing.
stories.summary: Bukele filed on the night of 19 November with Vice President Felix Ulloa. The election is on 28 February 2027, and a win could keep him in office until 2033.
stories.heat: AP, Reuters, Al Jazeera, Washington Post, UPI, Haitian Times · velocity: medium, filed 19 Nov
detail: NEW since yesterday: the filing happened. UPI reports Bukele submitted his candidacy to the Supreme Electoral Tribunal on Thursday night, and the ruling Nuevas Ideas party said the tribunal approved it.

Congress, controlled by his party, passed constitutional amendments in July 2025 that allow unlimited reelection, lengthen terms from five to six years and remove runoffs. Opponents and international observers say his continued rule is illegal. A CID Gallup poll from 24 to 27 October found 94% approval, UPI reports. The Washington Post and Haitian Times note scrutiny of his military operation in Haiti.

stories.title: The United States sold its first deep-sea mining leases, covering about 31.5 million acres of seafloor near American Samoa, to a single bidder.
stories.summary: Wetstone U.S. Ventures paid the $3 million minimum for each of two 20-year leases. The sale went ahead despite three lawsuits and a court ruling against the environmental review.
stories.heat: Ground News 109 sources (35% L / 49% C / 16% R) · Bloomberg, Mining.com, Samoa News · velocity: medium, sale 19 Nov
detail: The Marine Minerals Administration awarded the two leases on 19 November for $6 million in total. The leases allow only preliminary survey work; commercial mining would need further environmental approval. Reports differ on whether Norway's Adepth Minerals also bid.

The sale came days after a court ordered the National Marine Fisheries Service to assess endangered-species impacts more thoroughly. American Samoa has had a moratorium on deep-sea mining in its own waters since 2024 and, Samoa News reports, will not share in the lease revenue.

stories.title: The UAE called Somalia's expulsion of its ambassador 'escalatory and hostile'.
stories.summary: Somalia gave the UAE ambassador 72 hours to leave on 19 November and recalled its own envoy. Abu Dhabi answered on 20 November.
stories.heat: AFP via France 24, The National, Arab News, Asharq Al-Awsat, Al-Monitor · velocity: medium
detail: NEW since yesterday: the UAE foreign ministry said the move 'reflects irresponsible positions that undermine bilateral relations', The National reports, but added that the UAE remains committed to the ties.
Somalia accuses the UAE of backing regional governments opposed to Mogadishu, which the UAE denies. Somalia cancelled all agreements with the UAE in January, including port and security deals.

stories.title: Canada sees little movement from the United States on tariff relief, according to sources cited by Reuters.
stories.summary: Ottawa wants an interim deal to cut Section 232 tariffs on cars, steel, aluminium and lumber. Canadian negotiators argued on 19 November for a deal soon rather than waiting out Trump's term.
stories.heat: Reuters via US News, BNN Bloomberg, CBC · velocity: low-medium
detail: Reuters sources say trade minister Dominic LeBlanc reports little progress since talks broke down in August, when Trump imposed a 50% levy on $20 billion of Canadian goods. Carney and Trump spoke briefly at APEC without an announcement.

BNN Bloomberg reports that Canada's top negotiators said on 19 November there is no case for playing for time, but also no wish for a deal at any cost. Carney has said: 'If the U.S. doesn't want to do a deal, we're busy.'

stories.title: The Trump administration asked the US Supreme Court to let the EPA cancel $16 billion in climate grants from the Biden era.
stories.summary: Lower courts blocked the cancellation of Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund grants. The justices may consider the petition at their 4 December conference.
stories.heat: Ground News 31 sources (23% L / 54% C / 23% R) · AP via WTOP, SCOTUSblog, Washington Times · velocity: low-medium
detail: AP reports that a divided federal appeals court in Washington ruled in August that the grants were improperly ended. The government argues the Court of Federal Claims should hear the dispute; the EPA calls it the largest grant cancellation case ever. SCOTUSblog says the petition is listed for the private conference on Friday 4 December.

sections.title: Krieg
sections.blurb: Trump ties an Iran decision to 1 January and a bioweapons claim, Russia's 20 November barrage kills nine and drops missiles on Poland, and Saudi-led jets bomb Hodeidah as the Houthis threaten Jeddah.

stories.title: Trump says Iran may be working on chemical or biological weapons and that he will decide on new strikes after 1 January.
stories.summary: Trump told Fox News there is "indication" Iran is looking at gases and biological agents, and said the US would "wipe them out" if needed. Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected the claim and compared it to the 2003 Iraq weapons case.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing lead (7 stories from 1,857 articles) · CBS, Gulf News, Times of Israel, Bloomberg, NYT · velocity: high, new framing 19-21 Nov
detail: In a Fox News interview aired late on 18 November, Trump said: "They're looking at gases, looking at bio, because we've shut them out with the nuclear." He added "we'll see what happens after January 1" and "if it does happen, we wipe them out", CBS News reported.

On 19 November he told Israel's Channel 12 he was "not rushing to make any decisions on Iran" and could wait until next year. On 20 November he said Iran wants a deal but that what it offers is unacceptable, and linked gasoline prices to the talks (Gulf News, Times of Israel).

Bloomberg and The New York Times reported on 19 November that a new US strike is increasingly likely. The Times said Netanyahu is pushing for a four-to-seven-day campaign and that officials disagree on the intelligence about chemical or biological weapons, CBS said.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei compared the claims to Colin Powell's 2003 presentation on Iraq and said the allegations "keep changing". In Israel, opposition MK Avigdor Liberman said on 20 November there is no security reason to strike Iran now and that a strike would be politically motivated (Times of Israel).

sources.name: Times of Israel live blog, 20 Nov

stories.title: The death toll from Russia's 20 November attack on Ukraine rose to nine, and two Russian cruise missiles and a drone came down in Poland.
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Force counted 84 cruise missiles and 404 drones, and Zelensky said 27 ballistic missiles were fired. Poland's defence minister called it one of the largest Russian attacks with impact on Poland since 2022 and asked NATO for more aircraft.
stories.heat: Kyiv Independent, ABC (Australia), CTV, NBC · velocity: high, Poland fallout 20-21 Nov
detail: New since yesterday's edition: the full toll and the spillover into Poland. Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko reported 7 dead and 17 injured in Kyiv, and Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi reported 2 dead elsewhere. Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said 30 people were injured nationwide (Kyiv Independent).

The Air Force said defences downed or suppressed 79 of 84 cruise missiles, 3 ballistic missiles and 380 of 404 drones. Three Kyiv bridges were damaged (Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Pivdennyi and Darnytskyi), and the 750-kV Zakhidnoukrainska substation in western Ukraine was hit, forcing nuclear plants to cut output.

Two Kh-101 missiles fell at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem and a jet-powered drone at Molodycz in Poland. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the timing was deliberate, during Coalition of the Willing drills in Poland, and requested more NATO AWACS and F-35 jets. Swedish Gripens and a Dutch tanker supported Polish air defence.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned the attack. Trump said the missiles and drones landed "by mistake", and Donald Tusk criticised Trump for calling Putin "my friend", the Kyiv Independent reported.

stories.title: The Saudi-led coalition bombed Yemen's Hodeidah port on 20 November, and the Houthis threatened to hit Jeddah and told airlines to avoid Saudi airspace.
stories.summary: The coalition says it hit facilities used to smuggle weapons and ballistic missiles. The Houthis say coalition strikes killed 41 people in 24 hours, and the UN warned against further escalation.
stories.heat: The National, Gulf News, Al-Monitor (Reuters), Jerusalem Post, The New Arab, CBS · velocity: high, escalating 18-21 Nov
detail: Coalition spokesman Turki Al Malki said the "special operation" targeted port capabilities used for smuggling weapons and ballistic missiles. The coalition had told civilians to leave the port earlier on 20 November, and also struck sites in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz (Gulf News, The National).

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree had warned that Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports would become targets if Hodeidah was hit. The Houthis also called Saudi airspace unsafe for airlines, Reuters reported via Al-Monitor. The coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles fired at Jazan and drones over Riyadh.

Houthi media reported a raid on a power station in Mocha and a toll of 41 dead from coalition strikes over 24 hours (The New Arab). The Houthi health ministry also accused Saudi forces of attacking a civilian boat and killing 19 people. Neither figure has been verified, CBS noted.
Hodeidah is the main port for food and supplies into Houthi-held northern Yemen. Reuters reported on 18 November that Saudi Arabia expects the war to last into 2027.

stories.title: A Russian ballistic missile strike on central Kryvyi Rih on 20 November killed a 7-year-old boy and a paramedic and wounded 42 people.
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials say the paramedic was hit after arriving at the scene, and that Russia struck twice more with jet-powered drones during the rescue.
stories.heat: Ukrainska Pravda, UNN, Liga, Zmina · velocity: high, evening 20 Nov
detail: The missiles hit near residential buildings and a restaurant in the city centre on the evening of 20 November, Ukrainska Pravda reported, citing regional officials. A boy aged 7 died in intensive care and a 20-year-old paramedic died in hospital, according to UNN.

By 23:00 local officials reported 42 wounded, including four children, with 27 in serious condition (UNN). Officials said Russian forces carried out two more strikes with jet-powered drones while rescuers worked.

stories.title: Iran says it fired a surface-to-air missile at a US F-16 and an anti-ship missile at US-escorted ships in the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.summary: The claim followed a reported US missile strike near Qeshm Island, which Iran's Tasnim agency reported. The US has not confirmed any hit.
stories.heat: Gulf News live blog (citing Tasnim) · CBS, CFR tracker on Qeshm strikes · velocity: medium, 20 Nov
detail: Gulf News reported on 20 November, citing Iran's Tasnim agency, that the US carried out a missile strike near Qeshm Island, and that Iran said it fired at a US F-16 and at US Navy-escorted vessels. No outcome was given and the US has not commented.

A US official had described an earlier strike on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm on 17 November as self-defence against "IRGC aggression targeting U.S. personnel and assets", CBS reported. IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said Iran will not reopen the strait until US conditions are met (Gulf News).

stories.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say the Strait of Hormuz stays closed, while oil prices head for a third weekly fall.
stories.summary: Qatar called the closure an international crisis, and IEA chief Fatih Birol called it the largest threat to energy security in history. Oil rose on Friday but was set for a weekly loss as Middle East exports kept flowing.
stories.heat: CNBC, Marine Insight, Gulf News, CBS · velocity: medium, 19-20 Nov
detail: CNBC reported on 20 November that oil was on course for a third straight weekly decline because exports from the region continued. Marine Insight said prices rose after reports of tanker blasts near Hormuz and the Houthi attack on Riyadh.

The IRGC said on 19 November that two more tankers hit mines; this has not been corroborated, CBS said. The father of a Jordanian seafarer missing since a tanker strike appealed for a search. Birol's remark came on 19 November.

stories.title: The Pentagon told Congress the war with Iran has cost more than $48 billion since late February.
stories.summary: Deputy comptroller Arthur Miller gave the figure on 19 November, up from $47.1 billion in mid-October. Gulf News put it at $48.3 billion as of 13 November.
stories.heat: CBS, Gulf News · velocity: medium, 19 Nov
detail: Miller told lawmakers the total "includes munitions, equipment replacement costs, and operational cost", CBS reported. The same day the Senate rejected a war powers resolution 51 to 48, a vote carried in yesterday's edition.

stories.title: Ukraine says it struck the Kaleykino oil pumping station in Tatarstan, more than 1,000 km from the front, on 19 November.
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff says three 50,000-cubic-metre tanks were damaged and one caught fire at the station, which feeds the Druzhba pipeline. Ukraine also says it destroyed a Russian ballistic missile launcher.
stories.heat: Kyiv Independent (General Staff statement) · velocity: medium, 19-20 Nov
detail: The Kyiv Independent reported the General Staff's confirmation of the strike. Ukraine said it hit three Russian ballistic missile launchers overnight on 20 November and destroyed one, with damage to the others still being assessed. Russia had not commented in the sources read.

stories.title: Israel says recent strikes in Gaza killed three militants, including an Islamic Jihad commander, and Palestinian media report four dead in Bureij.
stories.summary: Palestinian media also reported a drone strike north of Nuseirat camp on 20 November. A Board of Peace official warned the body could hand Gaza to the UN if Israeli "intransigence" continues.
stories.heat: Times of Israel live blog · Al Jazeera, AP, Bloomberg on Board of Peace report · velocity: medium, 20 Nov
detail: The IDF said a strike in Gaza City on 19 November killed Thaer Al-Wadia, and that three operatives were killed in recent strikes in all. Palestinian media reported four killed in an airstrike in Bureij and two more in a drone strike; the IDF did not comment on those (Times of Israel).

The Board of Peace told the UN Security Council on 17 November that both sides have missed ceasefire commitments and that the truce could collapse (AP, Al Jazeera). On 20 November an official of the board said it would hand Gaza's keys to the UN if Israel keeps blocking progress, the Times of Israel reported.

sources.name: Times of Israel live blog, 20 Nov

stories.title: Iraqi security forces entered Jurf al-Sakhar, a stronghold of the Iran-backed militia Kataeb Hezbollah, under a compromise deal.
stories.summary: Under the deal, militia members are expected to move elsewhere in Iraq. Iraq was hit by US and Israeli strikes earlier in the Iran war.
stories.heat: Times of Israel, Gulf News, AP (Times Union) · velocity: medium, 20 Nov
stories.about: Kataeb Hezbollah is an Iraqi Shia militia backed by Iran. Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, has been closed to the Iraqi state for years.
detail: The Times of Israel reported on 20 November that Iraqi forces were set to deploy in the town, and Gulf News said they entered it the same day. AP described it as a compromise with the militia.

sources.name: Times of Israel live blog, 20 Nov

stories.title: Pakistani sources say Afghan Taliban forces attacked a Pakistani border post at Angoor Adda in South Waziristan.
stories.summary: Neither government has confirmed the attack. Pakistan's army said on 20 November that army chief Asim Munir visited the border area and was briefed on counter-terrorism operations.
stories.heat: Afghanistan International, Asia News Network · velocity: low, 20 Nov
detail: The two countries have clashed along the border repeatedly since 29 October, and a TTP attack on 11 November killed 10 Pakistani police, FDD's Long War Journal reported. No casualty figures were given for the Angoor Adda report.

stories.title: Estonia will close all road border crossings with Russia on 1 December after an attempted arson attack on a drone company.
stories.summary: The Kyiv Independent reported the decision on 20 November in its daily war roundup.
stories.heat: Kyiv Independent · velocity: low, 20 Nov
detail: The report links the closure to the attempted arson. No further detail was given in the source read.

stories.title: Sudan's army says its aircraft hit Rapid Support Forces headquarters in Nyala, South Darfur, on 19 November.
stories.summary: Military sources told Sudan Tribune the air campaign across Darfur and Kordofan is meant to weaken the RSF before a ground offensive.
stories.heat: Sudan Tribune · Al Jazeera analysis 14 Nov · velocity: low, 19 Nov
detail: The claim rests on army sources. Al Jazeera reported on 14 November that the army has taken villages in West Kordofan while the RSF holds al-Nuhud and all five Darfur states. AP reported that a 16 November army airstrike killed 13 people in Abu Zabad, West Kordofan.

sections.title: India
sections.blurb: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrives on 22 November for talks with Modi, Trump holds up India's low interest rates and 7% growth against the US Fed, the BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi over his Pakistan remarks in Chicago, the Sensex adds 898 points, and Congress wins Rajasthan's panchayat polls.

stories.title: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrives in India on 22 November for his first official bilateral visit and talks with Modi.
stories.summary: Shah's two-day visit is his first bilateral trip since Nepal's March election. Flood reconstruction aid, trade, energy and new air routes are on the agenda.
stories.heat: Ground News 18 sources (56% right) · Reuters via Yahoo, India TV, Outlook, India.com · velocity: rising, visit starts 22 Nov
stories.about: Balendra Shah, the former mayor of Kathmandu, became Nepal's Prime Minister after the March 2026 election. He has criticised New Delhi in the past.
detail: Reuters reported on 20 November that Shah will meet Modi on his first bilateral visit since the March election. India TV says the visit runs on 22 and 23 November, with talks with Modi on Monday 23 November, followed by a joint press conference and lunch.

Shah is expected to ask for Indian help to rebuild areas hit by Nepal's floods in August. Nepal also wants an extra route for commercial flights from the west to Bhairahawa, near Lumbini, and to Pokhara, Reuters reports.

He will also meet External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and call on President Droupadi Murmu. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and business officials travel with him. India.com reports that the leaders are expected to open India-backed projects, including the Nepal Police Academy, a bridge in Darchula and an integrated check post at Bhairahawa.
Outlook describes relations as strained and notes Shah's earlier remarks against New Delhi, which makes the tone of the visit a test for both sides.

stories.title: Trump pointed to India's low interest rates and 7% growth to argue that the US Federal Reserve should cut rates.
stories.summary: At a White House news conference on 20 November, Trump said the US could grow 14% to 20% with India's approach. Ground News flags the story as a Blindspot: no left-leaning outlet covered it.
stories.heat: Ground News 18 sources (0% left, 33% centre, 67% right, Blindspot) · ANI, India TV, NewKerala · velocity: high, remarks 20 Nov
detail: ANI quotes Trump: "If you look at India, they have low interest rates and they have a 7 per cent GDP. We'd have a 14, 15, maybe even a 20 per cent GDP." He said the Fed is political and keeps rates high when the government reports strong numbers.
India TV reports he said each percentage point of interest costs $650 billion. He did not say which period the growth figures covered or how large a cut he wanted.
The remark lands days before India's July to September GDP release on 30 November. Business Today and Dynamite News report forecasts of 7.2% to 8% for that quarter; the RBI projected 7.2%.

stories.title: The BJP called Rahul Gandhi a 'Pak fan boy' after he said in Chicago that India has become a side player in world affairs.
stories.summary: Gandhi cited Pakistan's role in US-Iran peace talks as proof of India's loss of influence. This is a new row, separate from yesterday's dispute over his 'sacred' or 'sick' democracy remark.
stories.heat: Ground News 15 sources (60% right) · PTI via The Federal, Deccan Herald, Outlook, Hans India · velocity: high, 20 Nov
detail: At the University of Chicago, Gandhi said India has become a side player in global affairs and pointed to Pakistan's role in negotiating peace between the US and Iran, PTI reports.

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari wrote on X: "Why is Rahul Gandhi so obsessed with Pakistan! At every global stage, Rahul acts like Pak Fan Boy!" He said Gandhi ignored India's peace efforts on Russia and Ukraine. BJP spokesperson Tuhin Sinha cited the Shimla Agreement and the Sharm el-Sheikh statement as past concessions by Congress governments.
Deccan Herald reports a second BJP attack over Gandhi's post mocking Modi about the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting. No Congress reply appeared in the reports read.

stories.title: The Sensex rose 898 points to 83,919.71 on 20 November, and the Nifty Bank index set a record high.
stories.summary: The Nifty closed at 25,800.60, a nine-month high, on a second day of gains led by banks. Foreign investors have put a record $12.21 billion into Indian shares in November.
stories.heat: Business Standard, 5paisa, HDFC Sky · velocity: medium, second straight rally day
detail: The Sensex closed up 897.96 points (1.08%) at 83,919.71 and the Nifty 50 up 286.30 points (1.12%) at 25,800.60, Business Standard reports. The day before, the Sensex had gained 990 points.

The Nifty Bank index rose 2.49% to above 64,500, a record. HDFC Sky describes investors moving money out of global AI stocks and into India, and 5paisa reports record foreign portfolio inflows of $12.21 billion so far in November. The Sensex fell to 82,403 early in the session after weak Asian markets, then recovered.

stories.title: Congress beat the ruling BJP in Rajasthan's zila parishad and panchayat samiti elections, by the count reported on 20 November.
stories.summary: Daily Jagran reports Congress at 599 zila parishad seats to the BJP's 301, with 981 of 1,275 results declared. In the panchayat samitis, Congress had 3,701 seats to the BJP's 2,181.
stories.heat: Daily Jagran, India TV live blog · velocity: high, counting 20 Nov
detail: Votes were counted in 37 districts on 20 November. Using State Election Commission figures, Daily Jagran reported Congress ahead with 599 of 981 declared zila parishad seats against 301 for the BJP, and 3,701 panchayat samiti seats against 2,181, with 7,393 of 7,543 declared.
The result is a setback for the BJP, which governs the state. In the 2020 rural polls the BJP won more zila parishad seats. Final certified totals were not yet published in the reports read.

stories.title: KL Rahul and Devdutt Padikkal took India to 239 for 1 at lunch on day three of the Wellington Test, 129 runs behind New Zealand.
stories.summary: New Zealand were all out for 368, with Henry Nicholls unbeaten on 175. Rahul was close to a century at lunch, and the second-wicket stand had reached 109.
stories.heat: Deccan Chronicle, Daily Jagran, cricketnews.com · velocity: high, match in progress 21 Nov
detail: New Zealand resumed day two on 317 for 6 and were bowled out for 368. Nicholls finished 175 not out from 335 balls; Glenn Phillips made 118. Jasprit Bumrah took 4 for 92 and Akash Deep 3 for 53, cricketnews.com reports.

India began day three on 159 for 1 after Yashasvi Jaiswal's 66-ball fifty. They added 80 without loss in the morning session to reach 239 for 1, Deccan Chronicle reports, with Rahul near his hundred and Padikkal past fifty. No stumps report was available when this edition was written.

stories.title: Modi tours West Bengal, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November and opens the 19.7 km Nitish Setu bridge over the Ganga.
stories.summary: In Bihar he unveils projects worth Rs 34,470 crore at Vaishali. He also attends IIT Kharagpur's platinum jubilee and a skills convocation in Lucknow.
stories.heat: ThePrint (PTI), PMO, Punjab Kesari, Amar Ujala · velocity: high, events today
detail: The PMO says Modi reaches IIT Kharagpur at about 9:45 am for its 75th anniversary and will talk with 75 students. In Vaishali he dedicates the Nitish Setu, built for about Rs 4,280 crore, and lays foundation stones for projects worth about Rs 14,450 crore, including four-laning of part of NH-139W, ThePrint reports.

Other items in Bihar are house handovers to more than 26,900 PMAY-Urban beneficiaries and 100 PM e-buses. In Lucknow he attends the fifth Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh, which honours 52 national toppers from ITIs and other training institutes.

stories.title: The Supreme Court rejected Karnataka's appeal to restore its ban on bike taxis and told the state to regulate them instead.
stories.summary: The ruling keeps the Karnataka High Court's order that lets Rapido, Ola and Uber run bike taxis. The court said motorcycles can be transport vehicles under the Motor Vehicles Act.
stories.heat: LiveLaw, Deccan Herald, Inc42, Siasat, Hans India · velocity: medium, ruling 19-20 Nov
detail: The court said a blanket ban is not allowed and bike taxis should be regulated under existing law, LiveLaw and Deccan Herald report. Karnataka had cited passenger safety, insurance and missing safeguards.

The decision upholds a January 2026 order of a High Court division bench, which set aside a single judge's ruling that had effectively stopped the services. The state can still write rules for the sector.

stories.title: India is charging an effective 162.5% duty and tax on bulk Scotch whisky, in the first big dispute under the India-UK trade deal.
stories.summary: Customs says the bulk shipments are concentrates, not whisky entitled to the deal's 75% tariff, and more than 80 containers are held at ports. The UK says ministers are working urgently on it.
stories.heat: Reuters via Business Standard, Business Today, Tribune, GTRI · velocity: medium, 18-20 Nov
detail: Reuters reported on 18 November, citing a government document and eight sources, that customs investigators classify bulk Scotch as compound alcoholic preparations at a 150% tariff. Diageo and Pernod Ricard say both bulk and bottled Scotch qualify for the 75% rate set when the trade deal took effect on 15 July 2026.

About 80% of India's Scotch imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk, Business Standard notes. The Global Trade Research Initiative urged customs to use the code in the trade pact. No settlement had been reported by 20 November.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan caused no major damage or deaths in Odisha, the state minister says, as its rain moves into Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
stories.summary: New since yesterday: Odisha reports no loss of life after the landfall near Gopalpur. Srikakulam and Vizianagaram stay on red alert, and the IMD warns of heavy rain in parts of Uttar Pradesh on 21 and 22 November.
stories.heat: Deccan Herald (PTI), Sakshi Post, Dynamite News, Amar Ujala · velocity: falling after landfall 20 Nov
detail: Odisha's Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said no major damage or loss of life had been reported. The IMD said the storm crossed the coast near Gopalpur with winds of 70 to 80 km/h, gusting to 90 km/h, Deccan Herald reports. India.com's live page reported more than 3 lakh people evacuated and 69 trains cancelled before landfall.

In Andhra Pradesh, Ichchapuram recorded 16 cm of rain and Kanchili and Kaviti 10 cm each, Sakshi Post reports, with red alerts for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram. Amar Ujala reports IMD heavy-rain alerts for several Uttar Pradesh districts for 21 and 22 November.

stories.title: A Tata Trusts board meeting chaired by Noel Tata on 20 November approved grants and did not discuss the listing of Tata Sons.
stories.summary: New since yesterday: the meeting left the RBI's listing demand to the Tata Sons board meeting on 26 November, which reports describe as a likely showdown.
stories.heat: Business Standard, UNI, Storyboard18, ETV Bharat · velocity: medium, board meeting 26 Nov
detail: UNI, citing sources, says the two-hour Sir Dorabji Tata Trust meeting did not take up the listing or a restructuring alternative. Business Standard reports grants of more than Rs 150 crore for five projects, including Rs 50 crore for a Pune hospital. Vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, who back listing, joined online.

The RBI's letter of 16 November told Tata Sons to follow the rules for upper-layer finance companies, including listing, but gave no new deadline, Storyboard18 reports. The Tata Sons board meets on 26 November.

stories.title: Ladakh votes on 21 November in its first panchayat elections since it became a Union Territory, along with municipal polls in Leh and Kargil.
stories.summary: All panchayat halqas and 38 municipal wards go to the polls from 8 am to 5 pm. The whole process ends by 30 November.
stories.heat: All India Radio, Ladakh government, UNI, Business Upturn · velocity: rising, polling today
detail: The last panchayat elections in Ladakh were held in November 2018, before it became a Union Territory in 2019, All India Radio reports. The Chief Electoral Officer set municipal polls for 21 wards in Leh and 17 in Kargil.
Leh district sent voting machines, ballot boxes and polling teams out on 20 November, Business Upturn reports. No turnout figures were available when this edition was written.

sections.title: Cinema
sections.blurb: Sunrise on the Reaping heads for a $110 million US opening, Ramayana Part 1 nears Rs 1,575 crore worldwide, O.M: Operation Mole gives Dhanush his biggest first day, and Michael skips the BAFTAs.

stories.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took about $51 million on its first day in US cinemas and is heading for a $110 million opening weekend.
stories.summary: Deadline's Friday estimate includes $21.25 million from Thursday previews, the second-best preview night of 2026. Lionsgate had forecast about $80 million for the weekend.
stories.heat: Deadline, THR, Variety, IndieWire, TheWrap, Forbes · Reddit feeds not readable this run · velocity: high, opening weekend under way
detail: New since yesterday's edition: the film has opened. Deadline's midday Friday update, reported by Dark Horizons, puts its first day at about $51 million, including $21 million from Thursday previews. That is the fourth-best opening day in the series, after Catching Fire ($71 million), the first film ($67 million) and Mockingjay Part 1 ($55 million).

Deadline now projects a domestic opening weekend of about $110 million, which would be the fourth-best start for the franchise. The Hollywood Reporter notes this is above Lionsgate's own projection of roughly $80 million. Dark Horizons, citing Deadline, gives an estimated $97 million from overseas markets.

The previews were $21.25 million, per Deadline as cited by ScreenRant. IndieWire says this is second in the franchise only to Catching Fire and second in 2026 only to Spider-Man: Brand New Day ($72 million). It also beat the $17.6 million previews of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey.
TheWrap reports a 67% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes against a 95% audience score. Some analysts expect the film to be front-loaded and to fall sharply after Thanksgiving week.

In the same weekend, Amazon MGM's I Play Rocky, a film about how Sylvester Stallone made Rocky, went wide to 2,447 screens. Dark Horizons, citing Deadline, projects about $3.9 million on Friday and about $11 million by Sunday for that film.

sources.name: Deadline: Sunrise on the Reaping opening to $110M
Dark Horizons: Sunrise on the Reaping scores $51M first day

stories.title: Ramayana Part 1 reached about Rs 1,575 crore worldwide after 16 days, by Sacnilk's estimate, and is closing in on Pushpa 2's Rs 1,742 crore.
stories.summary: Sacnilk estimates Rs 16.30 crore net in India on the film's third Friday, a 16% fall from Thursday. Its India net total is now Rs 880 crore.
stories.heat: Sacnilk, ETV Bharat, Koimoi, Variety (global chart) · Reddit feeds not readable this run · velocity: steady, third weekend begins
detail: New since yesterday's edition (Rs 1,547 crore after 15 days): Sacnilk's day-16 page, last updated at 10:16 pm IST on 20 November, gives Rs 16.30 crore net in India for Friday across all languages, against Rs 19.35 crore on day 15. That takes the India net total to Rs 880.05 crore.
Sacnilk puts overseas earnings at Rs 523 crore gross (Rs 8 crore on day 16) and the worldwide gross at Rs 1,574.60 crore. It says overseas figures are rough estimates.

ETV Bharat, reporting an earlier live reading of Rs 10.24 crore net from 12,925 shows, says the film is already ahead of Dhurandhar (Rs 1,307.35 crore worldwide) and still behind Pushpa 2: The Rule (Rs 1,742.10 crore). Koimoi had projected Rs 15 to 18 crore net for the third Friday from about Rs 4.70 crore in advance sales.
The Friday numbers came in on the same day that Dhanush's O.M: Operation Mole opened and took a large share of screens in Tamil Nadu and Telugu states.

sources.name: ETV Bharat: Ramayana day 16 eyes Pushpa 2

stories.title: O.M: Operation Mole, starring Dhanush and Mammootty, opened with about Rs 17.70 crore net in India, Dhanush's biggest first day.
stories.summary: Sacnilk estimates Rs 31.55 crore gross worldwide on day one. Reviews are mixed: critics praise Sai Pallavi and fault the rushed script.
stories.heat: Sacnilk, India TV, ETV Bharat, Glamsham, Outlook, The Week, THR India · Reddit feeds not readable this run · velocity: high, opened 20 Nov
detail: New since yesterday's edition (record advance sales): the first-day figures. Sacnilk's day-1 page, updated at 10:24 pm IST on 20 November, gives Rs 17.70 crore net in India from 6,628 shows: Rs 13.35 crore in Tamil (53.1% occupancy), Rs 4.00 crore in Telugu and Rs 35 lakh in Hindi (13% occupancy). It puts India gross at Rs 20.55 crore, overseas at Rs 11 crore and worldwide at Rs 31.55 crore.

Earlier readings were lower: India TV, citing Sacnilk at 8 pm, reported Rs 12.97 crore net, and Glamsham reported Rs 16.42 crore. Glamsham and others call it the biggest opening of Dhanush's career. ETV Bharat says it opened about seven times bigger than Dulquer Salmaan's Aakasamlo Oka Tara, released the same day.

Reviews are mixed. Outlook gave it 2 out of 5 and said Sai Pallavi, as police officer Nithya Reddy, gives the strongest performance while Dhanush and Mammootty are let down by the screenplay. The Week called it a derivative undercover story with a haphazard structure. The Hollywood Reporter India called it a morally complex drama that could have been a miniseries. The film is directed by Rajkumar Periasamy.

stories.title: Actor Samantha Ruth Prabhu and director Raj Nidimoru have had their first child, a son named Dev.
stories.summary: Samantha announced the birth on Instagram on 19 November with a first photo of the baby. The couple married in December 2025.
stories.heat: Pinkvilla, Bollywood Hungama, Deccan Chronicle, The Hans India, Prothom Alo · Reddit feeds not readable this run · velocity: medium, announced 19 Nov
stories.about: Samantha Ruth Prabhu is a Telugu and Tamil film star who also leads the Hindi series Citadel: Honey Bunny. Raj Nidimoru is one half of the director pair Raj and DK (The Family Man, Farzi).
detail: Pinkvilla reports that Samantha shared a photo of the newborn on Instagram, calling him 'our beautiful baby boy', and Great Andhra reports that the post gave his full name as Dev Nidimoru. Deccan Chronicle alone reports that the birth took place at Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai.
The couple married on 1 December 2025 at the Isha Yoga Centre in Coimbatore, Great Andhra reports, and The Hans India says a baby shower followed in September.

stories.title: The makers of the Michael Jackson biopic Michael have chosen not to enter it for the 2027 BAFTA film awards.
stories.summary: Variety reports that producer Graham King and director Antoine Fuqua made the call before the 19 November deadline. The decision does not affect the film's Oscar eligibility.
stories.heat: Variety exclusive, syndicated by Yahoo; ScreenRant on the Golden Globes ruling · Reddit feeds not readable this run · velocity: medium, reported 20 Nov
detail: Variety's Clayton Davis reported on 20 November that King, Fuqua and other stakeholders decided, after talking to Lionsgate and Universal, not to submit the film. Sources cited 'multiple factors' without naming them, and the companies declined to comment. The move takes Jaafar Jackson, Colman Domingo and the craft teams out of BAFTA contention.

King had earlier accused BAFTA and the BBC of 'cultural insensitivity and tone deafness'. Variety notes that the film, which opened to $217 million worldwide in April and became the first biopic to pass $1 billion, holds a 38% Rotten Tomatoes score and an A- CinemaScore. Separately, the Golden Globes refused the studio's request to place it in the comedy or musical categories, so it will compete as a drama.

stories.title: Actor Sharad Kapoor says Shah Rukh Khan called to offer help after Kapoor's public appeal for work went viral.
stories.summary: Kapoor, who played the villain opposite Shah Rukh Khan in Josh, told Navbharat Times he will meet Aryan Khan soon. He says Sonu Sood arranged doctors for his leg injury.
stories.heat: Pinkvilla, citing Navbharat Times · Reddit feeds not readable this run · velocity: medium, reported 20 Nov
stories.about: Sharad Kapoor is a Hindi film actor of the 1990s and 2000s, best known for Josh (2000).
detail: Pinkvilla reported on 20 November that Kapoor quoted Shah Rukh Khan as saying 'do whatever you like and wish to do; I am ready to help you.' Kapoor had posted videos about depression and a leg injury and asked the film industry for acting work, after an earlier video showed him giving away his four dogs.

Kapoor said Sonu Sood arranged a team of doctors for his leg and that he would travel to Karjat for further treatment. Pinkvilla links a separate report that Salman Khan and Sonu Sood offered financial help.

stories.title: Larry Poindexter, an actor in S.W.A.T. and many US TV series, has died at 66, five days after a car hit him in Los Angeles.
stories.summary: Variety reports that he died on 18 November before surgery for broken ribs. A car struck him as he crossed a street in Studio City on 13 November.
stories.heat: Variety (via Yahoo), several smaller outlets · Reddit feeds not readable this run · velocity: medium, reported 19 Nov
stories.about: Larry Poindexter was a character actor with roles in S.W.A.T. (2003), 17 Again, The Lincoln Lawyer, 9-1-1 and Days of Our Lives.
detail: Variety, syndicated on Yahoo on 19 November, says Poindexter was hit by a car in Studio City on Friday 13 November and died suddenly on the morning of Wednesday 18 November, before a planned operation to repair broken ribs. No official cause of death has been given. His television work also included NCIS, Criminal Minds, Friends and Melrose Place.

stories.title: Mumbai's Gaiety-Galaxy cinema complex reopened on 20 November after a 74-day closure.
stories.summary: Bollywood Hungama reports that the single-screen landmark in Bandra reopened with Ramayana and O.M: Operation Mole, four days before its 54th anniversary.
stories.heat: Bollywood Hungama exclusive; earlier closure covered by India TV, NewsBytes · Reddit feeds not readable this run · velocity: low, reopened 20 Nov
detail: The complex closed on 7 September. India TV reported at the time that police found its licence had not been renewed. Bollywood Hungama says the problem first looked like a simple licence renewal but dragged on for more than two months. The complex opened on 24 November 1972.
On reopening day, Gaiety showed Ramayana, Galaxy showed the Hindi version of O.M: Operation Mole, and Gemini showed Rajini: The Jailer 2, according to the schedule Bollywood Hungama published.

stories.title: Yesi Ramirez, head of casting at Disney's Searchlight Pictures, is leaving the studio after about six years.
stories.summary: The Hollywood Reporter says her exit comes as Searchlight restructures its casting department.
stories.heat: The Hollywood Reporter only · velocity: low, reported 20 Nov
detail: The Hollywood Reporter reported on 20 November that Ramirez is departing Searchlight, Disney's specialty film division, amid a restructuring of its casting department. This board read only the report's headline and summary, because the article page could not be opened.
